dedupe_keys.name: ensemble framework for flash flood forecasting ef5

description: EF5 is a distributed hydrological modelling suite created by the University of Oklahoma Hydrometeorology and Remote Sensing Laboratory for flash-flood forecasts. It combines CREST, Sacramento Soil Moisture Accounting or hydrophobic water-balance models with linear-reservoir or kinematic-wave routing. Configuration files select model parameters, precipitation, potential evapotranspiration and gauge locations. Users can generate streamflow and related hydrological outputs for basin to continental domains, with spatial and temporal resolution determined by inputs. The C++ source is public and free under the Unlicense, with compilation instructions for Linux, macOS and Windows cross-compilation. Its own manual describes ASCII, binary and GeoTIFF inputs, and a separate US parameter collection supports a FLASH implementation. The suite can support flood warning and infrastructure exposure studies. A limitation is documentation age: the bundled manual identifies 2016 version 1.0 and contains older model-support wording, while the README and article describe later combinations. No forecast, calibration or build was performed.
